newsitem.title: UK: HSE prosecutes, BJ Process and Pipeline.
newsitem.headline: HSE prosecutes, BJ Process and Pipeline.

text.p: The British government is to prosecute two oil services companies, AMEC Process and Energy Ltd (APEL), a unit of engineering group AMEC, and BJ Process and Pipeline Services Ltd for alleged breaches of health and safety legislation.

The case, due to be heard at North Tyneside Magistrates Court in North Shields on August 4, follows an investigation by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) into an incident in December 1995 in which three APEL employees were killed.
"We can confirm we have received a summons. We will be going to court," AMEL spokesman Jeremy McTeague told Reuters.
BJ Process and Pipeline Services were unavailable for comment.
The deaths occurred during high pressure leak testing of pipework and plant on a gas platform at APEL premises in Wallsend, North Tyneside.

APEL was the main contractor responsible for the building and commissioning of the platform, and BJ Process and Pipeline Services -- known at the time as Nowsco UK Ltd -- were subcontracted to undertake the high pressure leak testing.

The HSE alleges both companies contravened sections two and three of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 by failing to ensure the health and safety of their own employees and others present on the module.
The maximum penalty the companies face in the Magistrates Court would be 20,000 stg, but if referred to the Crown Court, a successful prosecution could result in an unlimited fine.
